items.title: Anthropic pledges 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund
items.why: Anthropic, maker of the Claude chatbot, said on 18 October it will commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund, subject to shareholder approval. The board may add 2% for every 50% rise in its value. The fund cannot be used for lobbying or political donations.
items.matters: Anthropic says the fund could help with job disruption from AI; the company is expected to list its shares this year.

items.title: China's economy grows 4.5% in third quarter, beating forecasts
items.why: China's economy grew 4.5% year on year from July to September, the National Bureau of Statistics said on 19 October, up from 4.3% the quarter before and above the 4.4% economists expected. Exports and factory output drove growth; property investment fell 20.6% in the first nine months.
items.matters: Weak spending at home in the world's second-biggest economy keeps China relying on exports, adding to trade tensions.

items.title: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro trade insults in first Brazil run-off debate
items.why: Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro clashed over corruption, the economy, security and healthcare in a televised debate in São Paulo on Sunday, a week before the 25 October run-off. Recent polls show a very close race.
items.matters: Flávio Bolsonaro, son of jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro, narrowly led the first round, 47% to 45%.

items.title: UN nature summit opens in Armenia with most biodiversity goals off track
items.why: The UN biodiversity conference, COP17, opened in Armenia's capital, Yerevan, on Sunday, with nearly 200 countries reviewing a 2022 pact to halt nature loss by 2030. A draft UN report says countries are off track on 22 of its 23 targets, Reuters reports. The talks run about two weeks.
items.matters: A central dispute is money: a UN report says funding for nature "falls far short" of the $200bn a year needed.

items.title: Ebola reaches eighth Congo province as Kenya confirms eighth case
items.why: Congo's health ministry confirmed two Ebola cases, one fatal, in northern Nord-Ubangi province on Sunday, the eighth province hit. Congo has recorded at least 9,400 cases and over 4,500 deaths since May, AP reports. Kenya confirmed its eighth case, a hospital attendant exposed to its first patient.
items.matters: The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment; all Kenya's cases are linked to one patient from Congo.

items.title: Sergei Loznitsa's Soviet archive film Imperium wins London Film Festival top prize
items.why: Imperium, a 175-minute documentary built from footage Italian cameramen shot across the Soviet Union in the early 1970s, won best film at the 70th BFI London Film Festival on 18 October. The first-feature prize went to Sompot Chidgasornpongse's 9 Temples to Heaven.

items.title: Japan set to launch probe to fetch soil from a Mars moon
items.why: Japan's space agency, JAXA, plans to launch its MMX probe from Tanegashima, in southern Japan, at 19:41 GMT on Monday. It aims to land on Phobos, the larger of Mars's two moons, collect at least 10 grams of soil and bring it to Earth in 2031.
items.matters: The samples could show whether Mars's moons are captured asteroids or debris from a giant impact.

items.title: Ukraine launches over 1,000 drones at Russia; Russian missiles hit Kyiv
items.why: Russia's defence ministry says it downed 1,015 Ukrainian drones overnight into Sunday; fires broke out at an oil terminal in St Petersburg, where the governor says one person was killed. Overnight into Monday, Russian missiles hit Kyiv; the mayor says a woman was killed and a metro station damaged.
items.matters: Both sides are striking energy sites despite the 'energy ceasefire' US President Donald Trump announced on 11 October.

items.title: Stampede at Durga Puja festival in India's Kolkata kills at least 19
items.why: At least 19 people were killed and 25 injured on Saturday evening when crowds at a Durga Puja festival pavilion in Kolkata, eastern India, rushed for cover from heavy rain, officials say. Police detained several organisers and security staff, and a judge will lead an investigation.
items.matters: Crowd crushes are common at India's mass religious gatherings; the state says about 58,000 Durga Puja events are under way.

items.changed: Updated: Davidovich Fokina won Sunday's all-Spanish final
items.title: Davidovich Fokina fights back to beat Jodar for Shanghai Masters title
items.why: Spain's Alejandro Davidovich Fokina beat 20-year-old compatriot Rafael Jodar 1-6, 7-6, 6-4 in Shanghai, China, on 18 October, recovering from a set and a break down. It is his first Masters 1000 title; Jodar needed treatment on his thighs in the final set.
items.matters: He had lost his first five tour finals; he now rises to a career-high 13th in the world.

items.title: Tonga beat England for the first time at Rugby League World Cup
items.why: Tonga beat England 30-12 in Perth, Australia, on 17 October in their opening Rugby League World Cup group match, their first ever win over England, AP reports. Haumole Olakau'atu scored two tries in front of a sell-out crowd of 18,302.
items.matters: Only two of six teams in the group reach the semi-finals, so third-ranked England must now beat France and Papua New Guinea.

items.changed: Updated: Chwalinska beat Kartal in Sunday's final
items.title: Poland's Maja Chwalinska beats Britain's Sonay Kartal to win Wuhan Open
items.why: Chwalinska came from a set and a break down to beat Kartal 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 in Wuhan, China, on 18 October for her first tour title, having beaten Iga Swiatek in the semi-finals. Kartal, ranked 170th, was the lowest-ranked WTA 1000 finalist since 2009.
items.matters: Chwalinska, ranked 146th in January, rises to 11th; Kartal returns to the top 50 and becomes British No 1.

items.title: IMF meetings in Bangkok end with warnings on debt and inflation
items.why: The IMF and World Bank annual meetings closed in Thailand's capital, Bangkok, on 17 October. IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva said low-income countries now spend 14% of government revenue on debt repayments, up from 8%. Reuters says nearly half of delegates walked out while Russia's finance minister spoke.
items.matters: Georgieva calls inflation 'a tax on the poor'; poorer oil-importing countries are hit hardest by the war-driven rise in energy prices.

items.changed: Updated: the Pope led Sunday's prayer from his window, his first appearance since surgery
items.title: Pope Leo leads Sunday prayer in first appearance since cancer surgery
items.why: Pope Leo XIV, 71, led the Angelus prayer from his window above St Peter's Square on Sunday, five days after surgeons removed part of his right lung to treat cancer. He told a crowd the Vatican put at about 15,000 that he would resume his activities gradually.
items.matters: Tests due this week will guide further treatment; his surgeon sees no medical reason to cancel November's South America trip.

items.changed: Updated: a tug was hit off the UAE; Iran says its seven-day reopening offer still stands
items.title: Gulf ship attacks continue as Iran says Hormuz reopening offer stands
items.why: UKMTO, the UK maritime agency, says a tug was hit by projectiles off the UAE on Sunday, two days after two tankers were attacked off Saudi Arabia. Iran's foreign minister says its offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days stands if the US lifts its blockade.
items.matters: About a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied gas trade passed through the strait before the war began in February.

items.changed: Updated: Macron refused the interior minister's resignation after a weekend of riots
items.title: Macron refuses interior minister's resignation after weekend of riots in France
items.why: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez offered to resign on Sunday after cost-of-living protests turned into riots and looting in Paris, Marseille, Lyon and other cities. The Élysée says Macron refused. The ministry says about 2,400 people were arrested on Saturday and almost 1,000 police and gendarmes were injured.
items.matters: Macron admits 'failures in anticipation and intelligence'; the unrest is seen as a test of the mood before the 2027 election.

items.changed: Updated: chip index's eight-day fall is its longest since 2008; futures rebound on Monday
items.title: US chip shares have longest losing run since 2008 amid AI doubts
items.why: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell for eight straight sessions to 16 October, its longest losing run since 2008, and lost 11.4% over the week as investors questioned AI spending. US share futures rose about 1% on Monday 19 October, and South Korea's Kospi, down over 17% in a month, rose.
items.matters: Goldman Sachs estimates five big tech firms will spend about $1.2 trillion on AI next year; investors doubt it will pay off.

items.changed: Updated: Brent eases about 2% after Trump waives Russia sanctions
items.title: Oil eases from five-month high after US waives Russia sanctions
items.why: Brent crude fell about 2% to near $108 a barrel on Monday 19 October, after touching $110 on Friday. Traders expect more Russian fuel exports after President Trump waived key US sanctions and tariffs on Russia. Attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz continue to cut Gulf supplies.
items.matters: Prices remain well above pre-war levels, keeping pressure on fuel, transport and food costs.

items.changed: Updated: tributes at Saturday's match; autopsy results still awaited
items.title: South African rugby player Hyron Andrews dies in France before match
items.why: Hyron Andrews, 31, a lock for Johannesburg's Lions, was found dead at the team hotel on France's Île de Ré on 16 October. Prosecutors say accidental death is the main line of inquiry; autopsy results are awaited. Players held a minute's silence before Saturday's match, which La Rochelle won 31-14.

items.changed: Updated: dengue toll now 348; measles deaths added
items.title: Bangladesh dengue deaths reach 348 as measles toll nears 1,200
items.why: Bangladesh's health directorate reported six more dengue deaths in the 24 hours to Sunday morning, bringing this year's toll to 348 from 112,400 cases. The country is also fighting measles: seven more children died, taking suspected and confirmed measles-related deaths to 1,196.
items.matters: Dengue, spread by mosquitoes, has no specific treatment; measles can be prevented with two doses of vaccine.

items.title: Indonesian shares fall to six-year low after MSCI downgrade warning
items.why: Jakarta's main share index fell about 5% on 19 October to its lowest since 2020, after an almost 12% drop on 16 October, its biggest one-day fall since 1998. Index provider MSCI says it may move Indonesia out of its emerging-markets group, citing opaque share ownership and weak enforcement.
items.matters: Being dropped could force global funds to sell billions of dollars of Indonesian shares; officials are meeting MSCI to seek answers.

items.changed: Updated: hotspots quadrupled to 1,104 on Sunday; Malaysia offers firefighting aircraft
items.title: Indonesia's fire hotspots quadruple as Malaysia offers aircraft to help
items.why: Fire hotspots across Indonesia more than quadrupled to 1,104 on Sunday, with Central Kalimantan, on Borneo, hardest hit, Indonesia's forestry ministry says. Malaysia has offered helicopters and water-bombing aircraft, but visibility below 50 metres may keep them grounded. Four firefighters died in East Java last week.
items.matters: Haze has disrupted more than 2,400 flights in Indonesia since August and closed schools in Malaysia's Johor state until 23 October.

items.changed: Updated: Champi passed just south of Guam on Sunday with no widespread damage reported
items.title: Typhoon Champi narrowly misses Guam and heads west over Philippine Sea
items.why: Typhoon Champi passed about 16 km south of the southern tip of Guam, the US Pacific territory, early on Sunday, strengthening into a super typhoon, the US National Weather Service says. Early reports show no widespread serious damage, and no deaths have been reported. The storm is now heading west.
items.matters: Philippine forecasters expect it to enter their monitoring area on Tuesday and possibly regain super typhoon strength.
